source.title: Tight Generalization Error Bounds for Stochastic Gradient Descent in Non-convex Learning
source.authors: Wen-Jun Xiong; Juan Ding; Xin-Lei Zuo; Qi-Zhai Li

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The experiments compare generalization-error bounds and report empirical generalization behavior under clipped SGD and varying network width, using a different method and measures from the listed versions.
record.gate_note: The text reports theoretical bounds and empirical experiments, but does not test random-label memorization, zero-training-error interpolation, optimizer comparisons, batch-size effects, dropout, magnitude-aware sharpness, or removal of memorized examples. The plotted bound values are not stated numerically.
record.test_reason: The study analyzes SGD generalization bounds and clipping, but none of its results tests V1–V8. Width sweeps measure bounds and loss gaps without establishing interpolation or falling test error. Its flatness term uses additive Gaussian perturbations without weight-magnitude scaling or the ranking comparisons required by V7.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors claim tighter SGD generalization bounds using T2pm-SGD, including an O(n^-1) trajectory term and an optimized O(n^-2/3) total bound under their bounded-loss assumptions. They report reduced overfitting with clipping and the stated width-dependent bound trends. T2pm-SGD is an analytical surrogate, so tighter bounds should not be paraphrased as improved performance from a new training algorithm.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies a theoretical perturbation-based bound for SGD and experiments on bounds and clipped SGD; it does not reproduce the interventions or measurements in the listed versions.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported bound varies with network width or filter count and perturbation noise standard deviation; clipping is tested at threshold 5.

fits_no_version.finding: The T2pm-SGD bound is reported lower and more stable during training than the T1pm-SGD bound.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For the tested MNIST MLP and CIFAR-10 AlexNet runs, the nonaccumulating perturbation analysis gives tighter bounds than the accumulating perturbation analysis.

fits_no_version.finding: The authors report that clipping gradients at threshold 5 reduces overfitting and improves generalization on CIFAR-10.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Gradient clipping can improve held-out performance in the reported CIFAR-10 training setting.

fits_no_version.finding: Bounds tighten with MLP width and loosen slightly with AlexNet filter count; empirical loss gaps are described as small and stable.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The tested generalization bound depends on architecture width without establishing corresponding changes in test error.

record.problems: The empirical comparisons are presented in figures without numerical values or uncertainty estimates. The reported width findings concern the bound, not a direct test-error sweep past zero training error. The text does not provide a numerical unclipped accuracy baseline for the clipping result.
record.rows_left_out: No additional reported outcomes relevant to the claim versions were left out. The paper's theoretical derivations and plotted results for trajectory and flatness terms are not separate measurements of the versions' named properties.

untested.parts: Matched random-label memorization and natural-label held-out performance, including chance performance with random labels.
Test error versus width beyond the width needed for zero training error in networks trained to convergence without explicit regularization.
Convolutional versus fully connected image-classifier performance, local connectivity, and initialization or learned-sparsity qualifications.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer performance under limited or broader tuning and recovery interventions.
Large versus small batches under fixed epoch budgets and adapted training recipes.
Controlled dropout comparisons, training-set-size dependence, and interactions with augmentation or weight decay. Using dropout in AlexNet does not test these effects.
Magnitude-scaled perturbation tolerance versus generalization gaps among similarly fitted networks, and ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Retraining after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: All row states are relative to V1–V8; cannot_determine does not dispute the reported bound or clipping findings. No cross-architecture comparison is available because the MLP and AlexNet use different datasets. Figure values cannot be recovered from the supplied text.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and held-out performance on natural labels.
Whether test error falls as width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error; the text reports bounds, not this test-error comparison.
Convolutional versus fully connected performance and the role of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer generalization under tuning choices.
Large versus small batch performance under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Dropout effects and interactions with data augmentation or weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and comparisons with norm- and margin-based measures.
Effects of removing memorized examples and retraining.

rows.subject: MLP on MNIST
rows.operation_detail: Compared empirical gap and generalization-error bounds for T2pm-SGD and T1pm-SGD during training.
rows.measure: Generalization-error bound and empirical gap, defined as the difference between training loss and testing loss.
rows.value: T2pm-SGD bound: figure only; text says it is consistently lower and remains stable, while the T1pm-SGD bound increases steadily.
rows.note: The text describes the plotted comparison but gives no numerical values.
rows.check: This compares analytical bounds, not a claim-version outcome. T1pm-SGD and T2pm-SGD are surrogate analyses of SGD, not separate practical training algorithms (Remark 1). The MLP depth is inconsistent in the source: Section 4 says three-layer; the Appendix specifies two fully connected layers.

rows.subject: AlexNet on CIFAR-10
rows.size_stated: five convolutional layers; appendix gives filter sizes 64, 128, 256, 512, 256
rows.operation_detail: Compared empirical gap and generalization-error bounds for T2pm-SGD and T1pm-SGD during training.
rows.measure: Generalization-error bound and empirical gap, defined as the difference between training loss and testing loss.
rows.value: T2pm-SGD bound: figure only; text says it is consistently lower and remains stable, while the T1pm-SGD bound increases steadily.
rows.note: The text describes the plotted comparison but gives no numerical values.
rows.check: This compares analytical bounds, not a claim-version outcome. The surrogate comparison does not establish better held-out model performance. The Appendix also specifies batch normalization, dropout at 0.5, and test-loss-based early stopping.

rows.subject: AlexNet on CIFAR-10
rows.operation_detail: Applied gradient clipping with threshold 5 during SGD training.
rows.measure: Overfitting and generalization performance; accuracy shown in Figure 2(a).
rows.value: The text says gradient clipping effectively reduces overfitting, resulting in improved generalization performance; accuracy values are figure only.
rows.note: No numerical accuracy or unclipped baseline is stated.
rows.check: The authors report improved generalization with clipping at threshold 5, but clipping is outside V1–V8. The supplied text gives neither numerical accuracies nor an explicit numerical unclipped baseline; observed cannot describe any listed version.

rows.subject: MLP on MNIST
rows.size_stated: width varied from 64 to 512; default width 512
rows.operation_detail: Varied MLP width and measured the T2pm-SGD generalization-error bound.
rows.measure: Generalization-error bound; text also describes the generalization gap as relatively small and stable across widths.
rows.value: figure only; text says the bound decreases as MLP width increases.
rows.note: The width result concerns the bound; the text does not report test error versus width or whether training error is zero.
rows.check: A decreasing upper bound and a small, stable loss gap do not establish decreasing test error beyond zero training error. Neither interpolation nor convergence across widths is established; the Appendix describes test-loss-based early stopping.

rows.subject: AlexNet on CIFAR-10
rows.operation_detail: Varied the number of first-layer filters and measured the T2pm-SGD generalization-error bound.
rows.measure: Generalization-error bound; text also describes the generalization gap as relatively small and stable across filter sizes.
rows.value: figure only; text says larger filter sizes result in slightly looser bounds.
rows.note: The width-related result concerns the bound; numerical values are not stated.
rows.check: Slightly looser bounds with more filters do not establish worse held-out performance. This convolutional width sweep neither tests V2's post-interpolation test-error prediction nor compares convolutional and fully connected networks on the same dataset for V3.
